entities.summary:
Pfizer Inc. is an American multinational pharmaceutical corporation founded in 1849 in Brooklyn, New York by Charles Pfizer and Charles Erhart. One of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies by revenue, Pfizer's development of the mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in partnership with BioNTech in 2020-2021 was the fastest vaccine development in history and among the most significant medical interventions of the 21st century.

Pfizer began as a fine chemicals company producing citric acid and tartaric acid, but pivoted to pharmaceuticals when it produced bulk penicillin during World War II through deep-fermentation technology, making mass production of antibiotics possible and saving millions of lives. Post-war Pfizer expanded into diverse pharmaceuticals, and its 1990s blockbuster drugs — particularly Lipitor (atorvastatin, the world's best-selling drug ever at $125 billion in lifetime sales) and Viagra (sildenafil) — made it a pharmaceutical giant.

The COVID-19 vaccine developed with BioNTech in under a year — using novel mRNA technology previously untested in approved vaccines — protected hundreds of millions and helped end the acute phase of the pandemic. Pfizer earned over $100 billion from the vaccine and antiviral Paxlovid in 2021-2022, the fastest revenue ramp in pharmaceutical history. Pfizer's subsequent acquisition strategy, including the $43 billion Seagen oncology deal in 2023, positioned it to lead in cancer treatments.
